db_evidence.notes: The clue_interval (73895-73903s) itself is fully retrievable and visually confirmed: a boss-health-bar frame at 73898s reads the beast's name, matching a hard boss encounter (episode/topic_facts describe 'boss fight in dark cavern with ashen flame-wreathed demon' at 73830-73890s culminating in an item drop '三味真火' at 73890s). However, this window contains the CHALLENGE itself, not a plant-gathering scene. The 'plant gathered on the way' has no unambiguous single match anywhere in episodes/topic_facts/object_states/entities/semantic_triples across the entire lead-up (60000-74000s): three candidate plant/herb events exist (火铃草 x2 gathered at ~64826s, confirmed visually; 九叶天芝草/九叶灵芝草种子 loot drops at ~65040s and ~71130s from combat, not gathering; a '药枣' inventory browse at 65910s showing an existing stock of 59, not a new gather). None of these, nor any other DB text, contains a token matching 'jujube' or '枣' tied to a gathering action. A direct SQL LIKE search for '%枣%' across episodes/topic_facts/object_states/entities/semantic_triples returns essentially nothing relevant to this scene.

root_causes: The reference answer 'fire jujube' does not textually or (as far as sampled frames show) visually match any plant/item name captured anywhere in the memory DB for this multi-hour lead-up window, so no rollout could have retrieved the exact reference term from the given tools/DB.

Two rollouts (3, 4) trusted a 30-sec episode caption ('大体草') at face value without visual verification; a sibling rollout's clip_qa call on the identical time window shows this caption is an OCR/captioning error -- the true on-screen text is '火铃草'.

Two rollouts (1, 2) conflated a post-combat loot/reward notification (九叶灵芝草种子, obtained by defeating an enemy) with the player actively 'gathering a plant', and this event is temporally far from the true clue interval (71130s reward vs. 73898s challenge).

The clue_interval given (73895-73903s) marks only the boss-encounter moment itself, not the antecedent plant-gathering event referenced by the question, so all rollouts had to search backward through a long, event-dense window with several superficially plausible 'plant gathered' candidates and no clear signal for which one is the reference's intended one.

Rollout 0 did the most rigorous work (visually corrected a caption error via clip_qa) and still scored 0, suggesting the reference answer may itself be keyed to game/localization knowledge not present in this DB's captions at all, or to a scene/plant this pipeline's automated captions never surfaced correctly.
what_worked: Rollout 0's use of clip_qa to re-verify a caption's item-name claim against the actual on-screen frame text caught and corrected a real caption error (大体草 -> 火铃草), which is good retrieval discipline even though it didn't yield the reference answer.

Rollout 3's SQL/semantic_search correctly located both halves of the causal chain (the plant-gathering scene at ~64800s and the beast-naming dialogue at ~70830s), showing the retrieval agents can link a distant antecedent event to a later named-entity mention across a large time gap.
transferable_lessons: For 'what item/plant did the player gather' questions, always visually verify via clip_qa before submitting -- 30-sec auto-captions can misread on-screen Chinese item-name text (confirmed OCR error here: 大体草 vs 火铃草).

Distinguish 'the player goes to gather X' (an active pickup of a resource node/plant) from 'the player receives X as combat loot/reward' -- these are different game actions and questions about 'gathering' should be answered from the former, not the latter.

When a clue_interval marks the culminating event (e.g. the boss fight itself), search backward through the full lead-up for the specific antecedent action asked about, rather than assuming the clue_interval itself contains the answer.

If a search for the reference term (e.g. a keyword like '枣'/'jujube') returns nothing anywhere in the DB despite exhaustive search across all evidence tables, flag this to the user/harness as a possible DB-caption coverage gap or reference-answer mismatch rather than assuming a retrieval failure.
